name: Conductite-QR
description: The first commercially available room-temperature superconductor in metallic form, Conductite-QR is a quantum-assembled yttrium-hydrogen-lanthanum alloy whose electron pairing mechanism is stabilized by embedded phononic resonators at the nanoscale, eliminating the need for cryogenic cooling. It carries electrical current with zero resistance at temperatures up to 85°C — covering the full range of habitable and industrial environments. Production requires atomic-precision assembly to maintain the resonator geometry, making it extraordinarily expensive and available only through licensed Apex Nanofabrication channels.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 neighborhood's power grid is mysteriously running at nearly 100% efficiency — someone has spliced bootleg Conductite-QR into the municipal lines, which should be impossible, but the energy savings are keeping the block alive through a brutal winter.

Apex Nanofabrication holds the only verified synthesis patent for Conductite-QR and has been quietly buying out or eliminating research teams that come close to independent replication — a dying physicist just sent her notes to the wrong person.

A Conductite-QR winding in a fusion reactor has begun exhibiting spontaneous magnetic flux pinning patterns that don't match any known physics — the patterns repeat, and one analyst thinks they look like language.
